requirements: Dogs from the United States entering Canada: (1) Dogs OVER 8 months old: only a valid rabies vaccination certificate is required — no health certificate needed. Certificate must be issued by licensed vet and prove vaccination within 3 years. (2) Dogs 3 months or older but under 8 months, accompanied by owner (1-2 dogs): only proof of current rabies vaccination required. (3) Dogs under 3 months: no rabies vaccine required, but proof of age must be provided to Canadian officials. (4) Dogs under 8 months unaccompanied: vet health certificate required (issued within 72 hours of arrival). (5) No quarantine required for dogs from the US. The US is treated as a low-risk / non-high-risk country by CFIA.
rows.notes: USDA APHIS page on US-to-Canada travel (last modified July 30, 2025) provides authoritative rules confirmed by CFIA. For dogs returning from the US that have also been in a CDC high-risk country in the prior 6 months, special rules apply — contact CFIA. No federal breed ban in Canada; Ontario and Manitoba have provincial breed-specific legislation (BSL) targeting pit bull-type dogs.

rows.estimated_cost_range: USD 0–300 federal (no federal fee); vet health cert: USD 50–200
requirements: No federal rabies vaccination requirement for cats from any country. Cats must appear healthy. No quarantine required at federal level. Airlines typically require a vet health certificate issued within 10 days of travel. Destination state rules may apply. Some states require a health certificate or rabies vaccination.
rows.notes: Cat import rules are consistent regardless of origin country at the federal level. USDA APHIS regulates cats but imposes no rabies vaccination mandate. State-level requirements vary significantly — e.g. Hawaii has strict quarantine rules for all incoming animals. Review_required is true because USDA sub-pages for cat-specific imports returned 404 and no dedicated cat import page was accessible; core rule (no federal rabies vaccine) is confirmed from the main APHIS page and known regulatory framework.
rows.source_name: USDA-APHIS
rows.source_quote: Animals entering the United States may be subject to regulation by APHIS and other Federal agencies. Depending on your destination State, your pet may need to meet State entry requirements in addition to Federal entry requirements. Pet owners are responsible for meeting all Federal and State requirements.

requirements: PLACEHOLDER ONLY — rules for exotic/other species (ferrets, rabbits, rodents, reptiles, birds, hedgehogs) vary significantly by species and origin. USDA APHIS and US Fish & Wildlife Service may both have jurisdiction. Full research required per species.
rows.notes: This is a review-required placeholder. Ferrets, rabbits, reptiles, birds, and rodents each have distinct rules. Some species (e.g. certain birds) face very strict USDA and USFWS import controls. Research required.
rows.source_name: USDA-APHIS
rows.source_quote: If your animal isn't listed below, it may not qualify as a pet and, therefore, may be subject to different import requirements by APHIS.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Inactivated or recombinant vaccine only; must remain valid through entire post-entry quarantine period. Must be given after microchip implant. Group 2 countries: rabies-free, no RNATT needed. Group 3 (most of world, incl. USA, UK, EU): continuous valid vaccination from RNATT blood draw to date of export.
rows.titre_test_note: Rabies Neutralising Antibody Titre Test (RNATT) required for Group 3 countries. Minimum ≥0.5 IU/mL. Blood sample sent to DAFF-approved laboratory (e.g. Kansas State University FAVN/RFFIT for USA origin). RNATT valid 12 months from blood-draw date. 180-day wait begins from date lab RECEIVES sample. Pet cannot travel until ≥180 days after lab receipt. For shorter quarantine (10 days), official identity verification by two USDA-accredited vets must precede blood draw; without it, 30-day quarantine applies.
rows.tapeworm_note: Two rounds of internal/external parasite treatment required; internal treatment must cover BOTH nematodes AND cestodes (tapeworms, e.g. Praziquantel or Fenbendazole). External: product must kill fleas and ticks on contact (oral systemics such as NexGard and tick collars not accepted).
rows.import_permit_note: Mandatory biosecurity import permit via DAFF BICON system. Apply after RNATT declaration received. Assessment typically 20–40 business days; can take up to 123 business days. Fee: AUD 626 (first animal), AUD 491 per additional. Cannot book quarantine until permit issued.
rows.quarantine_note: Mandatory post-entry quarantine at Mickleham Post Entry Quarantine Facility, Melbourne, Victoria — the ONLY approved facility. Pets MUST fly into Melbourne International Airport (MEL); no other Australian port accepts cats/dogs for quarantine. Group 2 countries: minimum 10 days. Group 3 with identity verification: 10 days. Group 3 without identity verification: 30 days. Estimated cost: AUD 3,114 for 10-day minimum quarantine (1 animal, DAFF FAQ 2025). Additional blood tests required for dogs from USA: Leishmania, Brucella canis (intact dogs), Leptospirosis. Canine Influenza (CIV) vaccination mandatory for dogs from USA.
approved_entry_points: Melbourne (MEL) — ONLY approved entry airport for pets requiring quarantine
rows.source_name: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry Australia (DAFF)
rows.source_quote: Your dog will stay at least 10 days in quarantine in Australia. Dogs must spend at least 30 days at the Mickleham post entry quarantine facility if the competent authority identity verification was not completed.

extras.cost_notes: Quarantine: ~AUD 3,114 minimum (DAFF 2025 FAQ) for 10 days, rising to ~AUD 6,000–9,000 for 30 days. Titer test (FAVN at KSU): ~USD 150–300. Import permit: AUD 626. Additional dog blood tests (Leishmania, Brucella, Leptospirosis): ~USD 300–500. Vet visits ×5+: ~USD 1,000–1,500. Health certificate + USDA endorsements: ~USD 500–700. Cargo freight to Melbourne: ~USD 1,500–4,000. Total for dog: roughly AUD 8,000–15,000 (approx EUR 4,000–8,000); estimate uses mid-range.
extras.key_deadlines_notes: Start process ≥6 months before travel for Group 2 countries; 9–12 months for most Group 3. Apply for import permit after RNATT. Cannot book quarantine before permit. Pets cannot arrive on Australian public holidays or weekends. 180-day wait from lab receipt of titer test sample is the critical path.
extras.health_certificate_notes: Official government health certificate required, endorsed by competent authority (e.g. USDA APHIS for USA origin). Must be USDA-accredited vet + APHIS ink endorsement. Travels with the animal to Australia.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Inactivated or recombinant vaccine only. Must be current at time of export and through quarantine. Group 3 countries (most of world): vaccination required and must remain continuously valid from RNATT blood draw date through export.
rows.titre_test_note: RNATT required for Group 3 countries (≥0.5 IU/mL). Blood must go to DAFF-approved lab. 180-day wait from lab receipt date. Valid 12 months. Group 2 (rabies-free): no RNATT required. Identity verification (two government vets) enables 10-day quarantine; without it, 30-day quarantine.
rows.tapeworm_note: Two rounds of internal and external parasite treatment required. Internal must cover cestodes (tapeworms); external must kill fleas and ticks on contact. Permethrin is TOXIC to cats — must not be used. Cats do NOT require the additional dog-specific blood tests (Leishmania, Brucella, Leptospirosis, CIV).
rows.import_permit_note: Mandatory DAFF import permit via BICON. Fee AUD 626 (first animal). Typically 20–40 business days; can take up to 123 business days. Cannot book quarantine without permit.
rows.quarantine_note: Mandatory quarantine at Mickleham PEQ Facility, Melbourne, Victoria (ONLY approved facility). Must fly into Melbourne (MEL). Group 3 with identity verification: 10 days. Group 3 without: 30 days. Group 2: 10 days (no RNATT needed). Cats have fewer blood test requirements than dogs. Estimated cost ~AUD 3,114 for 10 days (DAFF 2025 FAQ).
approved_entry_points: Melbourne (MEL) — ONLY approved entry airport for pets requiring quarantine
rows.source_name: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry Australia (DAFF)
rows.source_quote: Your cat will stay at least 10 days in quarantine in Australia. Cats must spend 30 days at the Mickleham post entry quarantine facility [if identity verification not completed].

extras.cost_notes: Quarantine: ~AUD 3,114 for 10 days. Titer test: ~USD 150–300. Import permit: AUD 626. Vet visits + vaccines: ~USD 500–800. Health certificate + endorsements: ~USD 300–500. Cargo freight: ~USD 1,000–3,000. Cats have lower costs than dogs (fewer blood tests required). Total estimate ~AUD 6,000–12,000 (approx EUR 3,000–6,000); estimate uses mid-range.
extras.key_deadlines_notes: Start process ≥6 months before travel for Group 2; 9–12 months for Group 3. 180-day wait from titer test lab receipt is the critical constraint. Permit must be issued before quarantine can be booked.
extras.health_certificate_notes: Official government health certificate endorsed by competent authority (e.g. USDA APHIS for USA). Must be ink-signed and embossed. Travels with the animal.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Schedule I countries (AU, NZ, UK, Ireland): no rabies vaccine required. Schedule II and III countries: valid inactivated or recombinant rabies vaccination required, in accordance with manufacturer recommendations (primary + boosters). Must be current at time of export.
rows.titre_test_note: Schedule II and III countries: blood sample for rabies serology must be drawn ≥28 days after a valid rabies vaccination AND ≥90 days before the date of export, and within 12 months prior to export. Must be conducted at a WOAH reference laboratory for rabies or at a laboratory in a Schedule I or II country approved by its Competent Authority. Minimum titre ≥0.5 IU/mL. Schedule I countries: no titer test required.
rows.tapeworm_note: Specific tapeworm treatment not separately mandated in AVS conditions; parasite treatment timing per schedule-specific conditions may apply. Dogs from some schedules require treatment documentation on health certificate.
rows.import_permit_note: Two-step licensing: (1) obtain dog licence first (before applying for import licence); (2) apply for AVS import licence ≥30 days before arrival. Import licence valid 90 days from issue. Also requires Customs In-Payment permit for GST. Border inspection appointment at Changi Animal & Plant Quarantine (CAPQ) must be booked ≥5 days before arrival.
rows.quarantine_note: Schedule I: no quarantine required if all conditions met. Schedule II (includes USA as of 2026): post-arrival quarantine NOT required unless: (a) pet arrives >5 days after owner, or (b) pet has been under owner/immediate family care <6 months — in those cases, minimum 10-day HOME quarantine applies. Smart collar tags used to enforce home quarantine. Schedule III: mandatory minimum 30-day quarantine at Singapore Animal Quarantine Centre (AQC). US reclassified from former Category C to Schedule II in 2025/2026 update.
restricted_breeds: Pit Bull (incl. American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier)
approved_entry_points: Singapore Changi Airport (SIN) — inspection at Changi Animal and Plant Quarantine Station (CAPQ), Changi Airfreight Centre
rows.source_name: Animal and Veterinary Service (AVS), National Parks Board, Singapore
rows.source_quote: The blood sampling must be done at least 90 days and within 12 months prior to the date of export. The blood sampling for rabies serology must be conducted at either a WOAH reference laboratory for rabies or at a laboratory in a Schedule I or II country/region approved by the respective Competent Authority.

extras.cost_notes: AVS dog licence + import licence fees (~SGD 90–150). Rabies titer test (~EUR 150). Health certificate + USDA endorsements (~USD 300–500 for USA origin). CAPQ inspection fee. Home quarantine: smart collar deposit/fees if applicable. AQC facility quarantine (Schedule III, 30 days): SGD 26.25–44.00/day per dog. Cargo freight to SIN: USD 800–2,500. Total for Schedule II origin (e.g. USA) without facility quarantine: ~EUR 1,200–2,500; for Schedule III with 30-day facility: ~EUR 2,500–5,000. Estimate reflects Schedule II (most Western countries).
extras.key_deadlines_notes: Obtain dog licence before import licence application. Apply for import licence ≥30 days before arrival. Book CAPQ inspection ≥5 days before arrival. For Schedule II/III countries: titer test blood draw ≥28 days post-vaccination, ≥90 days before export. Start 4–6 months early for most countries. Dogs at least 12 weeks old at time of export.
extras.health_certificate_notes: Official veterinary health certificate required. For USA origin: USDA-accredited vet + APHIS ink endorsement (original ink + emboss). Certificate must travel with pet as original endorsed copy. Issued close to export, within timeframe specified in schedule conditions.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Schedule I countries: no rabies vaccine required. Schedule II/III: valid inactivated or recombinant rabies vaccination required, per manufacturer recommendations. Must remain current at export.
rows.titre_test_note: Schedule II and III countries: rabies serology required. Blood draw ≥28 days after valid rabies vaccination, ≥90 days before export, and within 12 months of export. At WOAH reference lab or Schedule I/II country approved lab. Minimum titre ≥0.5 IU/mL. Schedule I: no titer test required.
rows.tapeworm_note: No separate tapeworm treatment mandated; general parasite treatment conditions apply per schedule. Timing must align with schedule-specific health certificate requirements.
rows.import_permit_note: Must obtain cat licence before import licence application. AVS import licence required ≥30 days before arrival; valid 90 days. Maximum 2 cats per HDB flat (up to 3 total cats/dogs in non-HDB). Customs In-Payment permit also required. CAPQ inspection booked ≥5 days before arrival.
rows.quarantine_note: Schedule I: no quarantine if all conditions met. Schedule II: no quarantine required unless pet arrives >5 days after owner or pet has been under direct care <6 months — then minimum 10-day home quarantine. Schedule III: minimum 30-day facility quarantine at Animal Quarantine Centre (AQC). Cats from most Western countries fall under Schedule II (no facility quarantine for personal imports in standard scenarios).
restricted_breeds: First to fourth generation Bengal cat crosses (from Prionailurus bengalensis)
First to fourth generation Savannah cat crosses (from Leptailurus serval)
approved_entry_points: Singapore Changi Airport (SIN) — inspection at CAPQ, Changi Airfreight Centre
rows.source_name: Animal and Veterinary Service (AVS), National Parks Board, Singapore
rows.source_quote: Your dog/cat must be at least twelve (12) weeks of age at the time of export. Ensure that your dog or cat is microchipped according to International Standards Organisation (ISO) Standard 11784 or ISO Standard 11785 Annex A.

extras.cost_notes: AVS cat licence + import licence (~SGD 50–100). Rabies titer test (~EUR 150). Health certificate + endorsements (~USD 300–500). CAPQ inspection. Home quarantine smart collar fees if applicable. Cargo freight: USD 800–2,000. Total for Schedule II origin without facility quarantine: ~EUR 1,000–2,200. AQC 30-day quarantine for Schedule III: SGD 16.80–26.25/day.
extras.key_deadlines_notes: Cat licence before import licence. Import licence ≥30 days before arrival. CAPQ appointment ≥5 days before arrival. Titer test blood draw ≥28 days post-vaccination, ≥90 days before export. Cats must be ≥12 weeks at export.
extras.health_certificate_notes: Official veterinary health certificate, government endorsed. For USA: USDA-accredited vet + APHIS original ink endorsement. Original must travel with cat.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Non-designated regions (most of world, incl. USA, UK, EU): at least TWO rabies vaccinations required. First vaccination: dog must be ≥91 days old (day of birth = day 0). Second vaccination: ≥30 days after first, within effective period of first. Must be inactivated (killed) or recombinant vaccine — RNA/mRNA vaccines and modified live vaccines are NOT accepted. Vaccinations must remain current (within effective period) through arrival in Japan. Designated regions (rabies-free territories): fewer steps and shorter/no waiting period may apply.
rows.titre_test_note: Mandatory for non-designated regions. Blood drawn ≥30 days after 2nd rabies vaccination (same day as 2nd vaccination also acceptable per MAFF). Must be sent to MAFF-designated laboratory (list on maff.go.jp/aqs). Result must be ≥0.5 IU/mL. Test valid 2 years from blood-draw date. 180-DAY WAITING PERIOD begins from blood-draw date (day 0); pet cannot enter Japan until 180 days have elapsed. If pet arrives before 180 days, it is held at AQS detention facility for remaining days (at owner's expense, up to 180 days).
rows.tapeworm_note: No specific tapeworm treatment required by AQS for import. General health examination required at time of health certificate.
rows.import_permit_note: No formal import permit required; however, mandatory ADVANCE NOTIFICATION (Form AC) must be submitted to Animal Quarantine Service at the expected airport of entry AT LEAST 40 days before arrival. AQS issues Form I (Approval for Import Inspection) in response. Bring Form I to airport. Early contact with AQS strongly recommended — bookings at major airports (Narita, Haneda) can be very tight.
rows.quarantine_note: If all requirements fully met (180-day wait complete, valid titer, valid vaccinations, correct documentation): quarantine at AQS is within 12 hours (typically same-day release). If 180-day wait has NOT elapsed: held at AQS detention facility for the shortfall days (up to 180 days total) — at owner's expense, cost can be very significant. Entry airports with AQS inspection: Narita International, Haneda, New Chitose (Sapporo), Kansai International, Chubu Centrair, Fukuoka, Naha. Pre-arrival AQS notification window: 40-day minimum; failure to notify causes entry denial.
rows.source_name: Animal Quarantine Service (AQS), Japan Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF)
rows.source_quote: Dogs and cats are required to arrive in Japan after 180 days have passed from the date of blood sampling for the rabies antibody test. If dogs and cats meet import requirements upon arrival in Japan, the quarantine period will be within 12 hours.

extras.cost_notes: Titer test at designated lab (e.g. KSU): ~USD 150–300. Two rabies vaccinations: ~USD 50–100. Health certificate + APHIS endorsement: ~USD 150–350. AQS inspection (within 12 hrs): minimal. Cargo/airline pet fees: USD 300–1,500. Total process for compliant dog: ~USD 700–2,500 (approx EUR 650–2,300). If non-compliant and held in AQS detention: detention fees can run several thousand USD for extended stays.
extras.key_deadlines_notes: Start process at least 7–9 months before travel for non-designated regions. Critical sequence: microchip FIRST, then 1st rabies vaccine, then 2nd rabies vaccine (≥30 days later), then titer test blood draw (≥30 days after 2nd vaccine), then 180-day wait from blood draw, then submit Form AC ≥40 days before arrival, then health certificate within 10 days of departure. Any lapse in vaccination during 180-day wait RESETS the entire process.
extras.health_certificate_notes: Official health certificate issued by government agency of exporting country, within 10 days of departure (for USA: USDA-accredited vet + APHIS endorsement). Electromagnetic health certificates from USA, Brazil, and Spain also accepted (as of March 2024). Certificate must show microchip no., vaccination dates, titer test result. Microchip numbers starting '900 202' are currently under investigation and not accepted.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Non-designated regions: two rabies vaccinations required (same as dogs). Inactivated or recombinant only — RNA/mRNA vaccines NOT accepted. Cat must be ≥91 days old at first vaccination. Second vaccination ≥30 days after first, within effective period of first. Japan inspects cats to prevent incursion of rabies (same legislative basis as dogs: Rabies Prevention Act).
rows.titre_test_note: Mandatory for non-designated regions. Same requirements as dogs: blood drawn ≥30 days after 2nd rabies vaccination. Must go to MAFF-designated lab. Result ≥0.5 IU/mL. Test valid 2 years. 180-day wait from blood-draw date applies equally to cats — cat cannot enter Japan until ≥180 days after blood draw. Non-designated region cats held at AQS for shortfall days if arriving before 180-day wait complete.
rows.tapeworm_note: No specific tapeworm treatment required by AQS for cat import. General health check on health certificate.
rows.import_permit_note: No import permit required; mandatory advance notification Form AC must be submitted to AQS at arrival airport ≥40 days before arrival. AQS issues Form I. Failure to notify results in denial of entry.
rows.quarantine_note: If fully compliant (180-day wait complete, valid documents): AQS inspection within 12 hours, same-day release. If 180-day wait incomplete: held at AQS detention facility for remaining days (up to 180 days). AQS entry airports same as dogs. Pre-booking with AQS is critical due to limited inspection slots at Narita and Haneda.
rows.source_name: Animal Quarantine Service (AQS), Japan Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF)
rows.source_quote: To import dogs and cats from non-designated regions, they must meet import requirements such as microchip implanting, rabies vaccination at least twice, rabies antibody test, and 180-day waiting.

extras.cost_notes: Titer test: ~USD 150–300. Two rabies vaccinations: ~USD 50–100. Health certificate + endorsement: ~USD 150–350. Cargo pet fees: USD 200–1,000. Total: ~USD 550–1,750 (approx EUR 500–1,600). Cats generally lower cost than dogs (fewer additional tests required). AQS detention if non-compliant: very costly.
extras.key_deadlines_notes: Same 7–9 month minimum timeline as dogs for non-designated regions. Microchip first, 2 vaccinations, titer test, 180-day wait, Form AC ≥40 days before arrival, health cert within 10 days of departure. Vaccination lapse resets the process.
extras.health_certificate_notes: Official health certificate from competent authority of exporting country, within 10 days of departure. Electronic health certificates from USA, Brazil, Spain accepted. Must include microchip, vaccination records, titer test result.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Australia (Category 1): different/minimal requirements. Category 2 (rabies-free, e.g. Hawaii, Guam): valid rabies vaccine required. Category 3 (rabies present but controlled, e.g. USA mainland): valid rabies vaccine required, must be given after microchip implanted, current at export. Under 2026 IHS (mandatory April 2027): official pre-export ID check ≥6 months before export; under 2021 IHS (valid through transition): no ID check required.
rows.titre_test_note: Rabies Neutralizing Antibody Titer Test (RNATT) required for Category 2 and 3 countries. Blood draw after microchip and after vaccination. Blood must go to approved laboratory. Result ≥0.5 IU/mL. RNATT valid 12 months. Australia (Category 1): no titer test required. For Brucella canis: dogs must be tested using RSAT, TAT, CPAg-AGID, or IFAT (2ME-RSAT no longer accepted as of 2026).
rows.tapeworm_note: No specific tapeworm treatment mandated in NZ import conditions as a standalone step; general parasite treatments documented on health certificate per MPI requirements.
rows.import_permit_note: Import permit from MPI mandatory. Apply by emailing animalimports@mpi.govt.nz at least 20 business days before permit needed. Permit application must include quarantine booking confirmation letter. Importer dog breed declaration required at entry.
rows.quarantine_note: All dogs except those arriving from Australia (Category 1) must spend minimum 10 days at an MPI-approved post-entry quarantine facility. Quarantine facilities are privately operated (not a single government facility); MPI maintains approved facility list. Space can be limited. Quarantine booking confirmation required before import permit is issued. Cats and dogs arriving from Australia follow a separate, simpler process. Entry ports for pets: Auckland (AKL) and Christchurch (CHC) ONLY — no other NZ ports accept live animal arrivals.
rows.source_name: Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI), New Zealand
rows.source_quote: All cats and dogs except those arriving from Australia are required to complete at least 10 days in an MPI-approved quarantine facility. Cats and dogs can only be cleared for entry at Auckland or Christchurch.

extras.cost_notes: Quarantine (10 days): varies by facility, roughly NZD 1,500–3,000+. Import permit fee: MPI charges apply (check mpi.govt.nz for current fee). Titer test: ~USD 150–300. Brucella canis test: ~USD 100–200. Health certificates + APHIS endorsements: ~USD 400–600. Cargo airfreight: USD 1,200–4,000. Total: approximately NZD 7,000–15,000 (approx EUR 3,000–7,000). Reddit reports ~NZD 7,000 for permits + quarantine + ~NZD 3,000 for flights/vet.
extras.key_deadlines_notes: Start 6–12 months before travel for Category 3. Sequence: microchip, rabies vaccine, titer test, 180-day wait (for some categories), book quarantine facility, apply for import permit ≥20 business days before permit needed, health certificates within required window before departure. Under 2026 IHS (mandatory April 1, 2027): official ID check must happen ≥6 months before export — start October 2026 if traveling post-April 2027.
extras.health_certificate_notes: Health Certificate A (issued by USDA-accredited vet, APHIS-endorsed) and Health Certificate B (issued and endorsed by APHIS) for USA origin. Separate Health Certificates A and B required. Laboratory reports must accompany documents. Crate seals no longer required for USA mainland/PR/USVI/Northern Mariana Islands pets as of March 1, 2026.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Category 2 (e.g. Hawaii): valid rabies vaccine required. Category 3 (e.g. USA mainland): rabies vaccine required, given after microchip. No original vaccination records required for cats from Category 2 states/territories. Australia (Category 1): minimal requirements.
rows.titre_test_note: RNATT required for Category 2 and 3 countries. Minimum ≥0.5 IU/mL. Blood at approved laboratory. Valid 12 months. No Brucella canis test required for cats (dogs only). Category 1 (Australia): no titer test required.
rows.tapeworm_note: No standalone tapeworm treatment mandated; general parasite treatment as per MPI conditions documented on health certificate.
rows.import_permit_note: MPI import permit mandatory. Apply to animalimports@mpi.govt.nz ≥20 business days before permit needed. Quarantine booking confirmation letter required as part of permit application.
rows.quarantine_note: All cats except those from Australia must spend minimum 10 days at an MPI-approved quarantine facility. Entry only at Auckland (AKL) or Christchurch (CHC). Quarantine facilities privately operated; book space early. Cost varies by facility and cat size; roughly NZD 1,000–2,500.
restricted_breeds: Bengal cats with <5 generations of domestic ancestry from Prionailurus bengalensis (must provide 5-gen documentation)
rows.source_name: Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI), New Zealand
rows.source_quote: MPI's current guidance says all cats and dogs except those arriving from Australia are required to complete at least 10 days in an MPI-approved quarantine facility.

extras.cost_notes: Quarantine (10 days): ~NZD 1,000–2,500. Import permit fee per MPI schedule. Titer test: ~USD 150–300. Health certificates + APHIS endorsements: ~USD 300–500. Cargo airfreight: USD 800–2,500. Total: approximately NZD 5,000–10,000 (approx EUR 2,500–5,500). Cats generally lower total cost than dogs.
extras.key_deadlines_notes: 6–12 months lead time for Category 3. Sequence: microchip, rabies vaccine, titer test, book quarantine, apply for permit ≥20 business days before needed, health certificates close to departure. From April 1, 2027: 2026 IHS mandatory with official ID check ≥6 months before export.
extras.health_certificate_notes: Health Certificate A (USDA-accredited vet + APHIS-endorsed) and Health Certificate B (APHIS-issued and endorsed) for USA origin. Lab reports must accompany documents. No crate seals required for USA mainland/PR/USVI/NMI cats as of March 1, 2026.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Valid rabies vaccination required. Must be given ≥21 days before travel. Dog must be ≥12 weeks old at time of vaccination. Vaccine must remain valid at time of UAE arrival. Core vaccinations also required: Canine Distemper, Canine Parvovirus, Infectious Canine Hepatitis, Leptospirosis (icterohaemorrhagiae and canicola). Pet must be ≥15 weeks old at time of import.
rows.titre_test_note: Rabies titer test ≥0.5 IU/mL required (documented on health certificate). Blood sample collected ≤12 months prior to travel. If first-time vaccination or lapsed vaccination: blood collected ≥21 days after vaccination. If valid booster ongoing: blood can be collected same day or after most recent vaccination. Approved lab (e.g. Kansas State University VDL for USA origin).
rows.tapeworm_note: External and internal parasite treatment required within 14 days prior to travel. External: Fipronil or Permethrin recommended. Internal: Praziquantel recommended. All documented on health certificate.
rows.import_permit_note: Import permit from UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) is mandatory before travel. Apply online via MOCCAE digital services (ds.moccae.gov.ae). Import permit valid 30 days (some sources indicate 90 days — verify at time of application). Permit fee: ~AED 200. Maximum: 2 dogs OR 2 cats OR 1 dog + 1 cat per import annually. Pets travel as manifested cargo only (in-cabin not permitted). Emirate-specific registration may be required post-arrival (Dubai Municipality, Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority).
rows.quarantine_note: No mandatory quarantine for compliant pets. Upon arrival, MOCCAE veterinary officer inspects documents and scans microchip; compliant pets released to owner. Non-compliant pets may be held, returned, or subject to penalties. Vet inspection at port of entry: Dubai Cargo Village or Abu Dhabi cargo terminal.
restricted_breeds: Pit Bull Terrier (all variants, incl. American Pit Bull Terrier)
approved_entry_points: Dubai International Airport (DXB) — primary entry via Emirates SkyCargo at Dubai Cargo Village
Abu Dhabi International Airport (AUH) — Zayed International cargo terminal
rows.source_name: UAE Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) via USDA APHIS export guidance
rows.source_quote: Before traveling with your pet, you must obtain an import permit from the UAE's Ministry of Climate Change and Environment. This import permit is valid for 30 days. Your pet will not be allowed to enter the UAE with an expired import permit.

extras.cost_notes: MOCCAE import permit: ~AED 200 (~EUR 50). Rabies titer test: ~USD 150–300. Health certificate + government endorsement (USDA APHIS): ~USD 150–350. Core vaccinations + parasite treatment: ~USD 100–200. Cargo airline fee: USD 300–1,500. Emirate registration post-arrival: varies. No quarantine cost. Total estimate: ~USD 900–2,500 (approx EUR 800–2,300). Generally the lowest-cost of the 5 countries researched.

provenance_json.notes: MOCCAE direct URL returned 404; information sourced via USDA APHIS official UAE pet guidance (T1) and MOCCAE breed ban documentation (T1 by verification). Confidence slightly reduced due to inability to directly load moccae.gov.ae pet import page.

extras.key_deadlines_notes: If pet needs new vaccination and titer test: allow 8–12 weeks minimum. Sequence: ISO microchip (before vaccination), rabies + core vaccines, 21-day wait, titer test blood draw, 2–3 week lab processing, MOCCAE import permit application, permit issuance (days to weeks), health certificate within 10 days of departure, USDA/government endorsement. Import permit must be obtained BEFORE health certificate is finalized.
extras.health_certificate_notes: Official health certificate from accredited veterinarian, endorsed by national authority (e.g. USDA APHIS ink-signed and embossed for USA). Health certificate valid 10 days after issuance. Must include: microchip, all vaccinations (with manufacturer, batch, dates), parasite treatment records, rabies titer test result. UAE also requires Annex No. 3 'Model of Veterinary Health Certificate for Exporting Cats and Dogs into the UAE' format.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Valid rabies vaccination required, given ≥21 days before travel. Cat must be ≥12 weeks old at vaccination. Vaccine must be valid at UAE arrival. Core vaccinations also required: Feline Panleukopenia, Feline Rhinotracheitis (Herpesvirus-1), Feline Calicivirus. Cat must be ≥15 weeks old at import.
rows.titre_test_note: Rabies antibody titer test ≥0.5 IU/mL required and documented on health certificate. Blood sample ≤12 months before travel. First-time/lapsed: blood ≥21 days after vaccination. Valid ongoing booster: blood can be same day or after most recent vaccination. Approved lab required.
rows.tapeworm_note: External and internal parasite treatment within 14 days prior to travel. External: Fipronil recommended (Permethrin is TOXIC to cats — must NOT be used). Internal: Praziquantel recommended. Documented on health certificate.
rows.import_permit_note: MOCCAE import permit mandatory before travel. Apply online at ds.moccae.gov.ae. Valid 30 days. Fee ~AED 200. Maximum 2 cats (or combined 1 cat + 1 dog) per import annually. Cats travel as manifested cargo. Post-arrival registration may apply in specific emirates.
rows.quarantine_note: No mandatory quarantine for compliant cats. MOCCAE vet inspection on arrival at cargo terminal. Compliant cats released to owner after document check and microchip scan. Non-compliant cats may be returned at owner's expense.
restricted_breeds: First to fourth generation Bengal cat crosses (from Prionailurus bengalensis — must show 5-generation pedigree)
First to fourth generation Savannah cat crosses (from Leptailurus serval — must show 5-generation pedigree)
approved_entry_points: Dubai International Airport (DXB) — Dubai Cargo Village
Abu Dhabi International Airport (AUH) — Zayed International cargo terminal

extras.cost_notes: MOCCAE import permit: ~AED 200 (~EUR 50). Titer test: ~USD 150–300. Health certificate + endorsement: ~USD 150–350. Core vaccinations + parasite treatment: ~USD 80–150. Valid rabies vaccination administered by an authorised veterinarian when the animal was at least 12 weeks old; vaccination valid not less than 21 days after completion of the primary vaccination protocol

EU Pet Passport (for pets travelling from an EU member state or Northern Ireland) OR an official EU Animal Health Certificate (for pets from non-EU/third countries), issued and endorsed by an official veterinarian; certificate valid for 10 days from date of issue until documentary/identity check at the EU travellers' point of entry

requirements: All dogs entering the US (including returning US resident dogs) must be accompanied by a completed CDC Dog Import Form receipt — submitted online at no cost, valid for a single entry on the listed arrival date (or up to 6 months for dogs from low-risk/rabies-free countries)
Dogs must be at least 6 months old at the time of entry into the United States
Dogs must be microchipped with a chip detectable by a universal scanner; microchip must be implanted BEFORE rabies vaccination or the vaccination will be invalid
Dogs must appear healthy upon arrival

FROM DOG RABIES-FREE OR LOW-RISK COUNTRIES ONLY (e.g., Canada, Australia, UK, EU countries): CDC Dog Import Form receipt is the only required document; no rabies vaccination certificate or health certificate required by CDC (USDA/state rules may still apply)

FROM HIGH-RISK COUNTRIES — US-VACCINATED DOGS: Must have both the CDC Dog Import Form receipt AND a Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination form, completed by a USDA-accredited veterinarian before the dog departs the US and endorsed by USDA; USDA-endorsed export health certificates issued after July 31, 2025 are no longer accepted for re-entry in place of this form

FROM HIGH-RISK COUNTRIES — FOREIGN-VACCINATED DOGS: Must have CDC Dog Import Form receipt, Certification of Foreign Rabies Vaccination and Microchip form (completed by vet and endorsed by an official government veterinarian in the origin country), a valid rabies serology titer from a CDC-approved laboratory, AND a reservation at a CDC-registered animal care facility; if no valid titer, a 28-day quarantine reservation at the CDC-registered facility is required; dog may only arrive at the US airport associated with the registered facility
USDA APHIS and individual US state regulations may impose additional requirements (health certificates, state entry permits, specific breed restrictions at state level)
rows.notes: CDC 2024 dog import rule change (effective August 1, 2024): Simplified requirements for dogs from dog rabies-free or low-risk countries — CDC Dog Import Form receipt is the only federal document required. Dogs from high-risk countries with foreign vaccination require pre-arranged CDC-registered facility reservation and, without a valid titer, a mandatory 28-day facility quarantine at owner's expense. Cats do NOT require rabies vaccination for US entry. No federal breed ban exists, but US states and municipalities have breed-specific legislation (e.g., pit bull restrictions in certain cities). Dogs cannot enter the US unvaccinated from high-risk countries — entry will be denied. High-risk country list: visit cdc.gov/importation/dogs/high-risk-countries.html.

Cats must appear healthy upon arrival; CDC recommends (but does not federally mandate) that all cats be vaccinated against rabies
No CDC documentation form is required for cats (unlike dogs)
Some US states require proof of rabies vaccination for cats entering the state — check specific destination state requirements
Airlines may require a health certificate issued within 10 days of travel; check with your specific airline
USDA APHIS has no special import health certificate requirement for cats entering as personal pets from most countries
If travelling with more than two cats or for commercial purposes, additional USDA APHIS regulations may apply
rows.notes: The US has no federal quarantine or rabies vaccination requirement for cats. This is notably more permissive than dogs. State-level requirements vary — some states require current rabies vaccination certificates for cats. Airline-specific health certificate requirements are separate from federal import rules. CDC strongly recommends rabies vaccination even though it is not federally mandated for cats.

requirements: Dogs 3 months of age or older: valid rabies vaccination certificate, issued by a licensed veterinarian, in English or French (certificate only in Spanish may be rejected by CBSA); certificate must clearly identify the animal and confirm the vaccine is current; Canada recognises 1-year and 3-year rabies vaccines (if no validity date appears on the certificate, it is treated as a 1-year vaccine)
Dogs under 3 months of age: exempt from rabies vaccination requirement; proof of age must be available for CBSA inspection

Dogs older than 8 months accompanied by their owner: proof of current rabies vaccination is all that is required — no health certificate needed for personal pets from most countries (USDA APHIS confirms this for US-to-Canada travel)

Dogs from the 9 CFIA-recognised rabies-free countries (Australia, Fiji, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Japan, New Zealand, Sweden, United Kingdom): instead of a rabies vaccination certificate, a veterinary certificate confirming the country has been free of rabies for the preceding 6 months and that the dog has resided there for the same period or since birth is required; must be in English or French
No mandatory rabies titre test (RNATT) for personal pets; RNATT exists as an alternative pathway but is not the standard traveller requirement
No import permit required for personal accompanied pets (1–2 dogs accompanied by their owner)

CBSA (Canada Border Services Agency) performs a documentary and visual health inspection at the port of entry; CFIA inspection fee applies (approximately CAD $36.95 for first animal, $6.16 for each additional animal — confirm current rates with CBSA)

Dogs under 8 months travelling unaccompanied (without owner): require a health certificate issued by a licensed veterinarian within 72 hours of arrival in Canada, plus vaccination against distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus and parainfluenza (from at least 6 weeks of age)

Important: No dogs from countries classified as high-risk for canine rabies may be commercially imported into Canada since September 28, 2022; this restriction applies to commercial shipments (sale, adoption, rescue, breeding) but NOT personal pets accompanying their owner
rows.notes: Canada is relatively permissive for personal pet dogs. No quarantine for pets meeting requirements. Microchip is strongly recommended (ISO 11784/11785) but not legally mandated for personal pets. EU Pet Passport is accepted as proof of rabies vaccination. Certificate must be in English or French. Canada's rabies-free country list (9 countries only) is shorter than the EU's — Norway and the US are NOT on the list, so dogs from those countries require a rabies vaccination certificate. Dogs from New Mexico or Texas with travel within the past 21 days may not be eligible for import (check current CFIA advisories). State-level breed bans in Canadian provinces (e.g., Ontario banned pit bulls) may apply — verify with the destination province.

requirements: Cats 3 months of age or older: valid rabies vaccination certificate, issued by a licensed veterinarian, in English or French; certificate must clearly identify the animal and confirm the vaccine is current
Cats under 3 months of age: exempt from import requirements when travelling with their owner; proof of age should be available

Cats from the 9 CFIA-recognised rabies-free countries (Australia, Fiji, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Japan, New Zealand, Sweden, United Kingdom): veterinary certificate confirming the country has been free of rabies for the preceding 6 months and the cat has resided there during that period or since birth, in English or French; OR proof of current rabies vaccination (EU Pet Passport accepted)
No mandatory rabies titre test for personal pet cats
No import permit required for personal accompanied cats
CBSA performs a documentary and visual health inspection at the port of entry; CFIA inspection fee applies
Wolf-cat hybrids (Savannah, Bengal cats not 5th-generation removed from the wild) cannot be imported under standard personal pet regulations; check CFIA for hybrid cat import rules
No breed restrictions for domestic cats at federal level
rows.notes: Same framework as dogs for cats: from a CFIA rabies-free country, a certificate of rabies-free origin suffices; from all other countries, a rabies vaccination certificate in English or French is required. No quarantine, no titre test, no import permit for personal pet cats. EU Pet Passport accepted as proof of vaccination. Microchip strongly recommended but not mandated. Cats under 3 months are fully exempt from import requirements when accompanying their owner.

rows.microchip_standard: ISO 11784 / ISO 11785 Annex A transponder. A tattoo is accepted only if applied before 3 July 2011 and still clearly legible. Identification must be done BEFORE the rabies vaccination for the vaccination to be recognised as valid.
rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Primary vaccination only valid if given at 12 weeks of age or older AND after identification; it becomes valid 21 days (3 weeks) after the first injection. Boosters must follow the periodicity of the vaccine used. Combined with the French minimum entry age this means the animal is at least 15 weeks old on arrival.
rows.titre_test_note: No rabies antibody titration is required for movements from another EU Member State or from an EEA state whose movements are regulated as intra-EU. Norway is such a case: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1293 recital 3 removed Norway from the Annex II third-country list because 'Decision of the EEA Joint Committee No 66/2016 regulates the non-commercial movement into a Member State of dogs, cats and ferrets from Norway' — i.e. a Norway→France move follows the intra-EU rules, not the third-country protocol.
rows.tapeworm_note: France does NOT require an anti-echinococcus (tapeworm) treatment on entry. The 24–120 hour praziquantel window applies to dogs entering Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway and the United Kingdom — not to dogs entering France. A mover leaving Norway therefore drops this step in the outbound direction.
rows.health_cert_type: Valid EU pet passport issued by an authorised veterinarian (model in Part 1 of Annex III to Regulation (EU) 577/2013). Passports issued in Norway comply with the same model, with national cover adaptations, from 1 June 2016; passports issued before 29 December 2014 (EU) or 1 June 2016 (Norway) under Decision 2003/803/EC remain valid.
rows.quarantine_note: No quarantine for a compliant animal. If an anomaly is found when the animal is registered with I-CAD, the file goes to the departmental DDPP, which can place the animal under official surveillance by prefectoral order; vaccinating an animal under surveillance is prohibited until the period ends, and the definitive identification card is only issued at the end of it.
banned_breeds: Crossbreeds morphologically assimilable to American Staffordshire terrier / pit-bull without pedigree — 1st category
Crossbreeds morphologically assimilable to Mastiff / boerbull without pedigree — 1st category
Crossbreeds morphologically assimilable to Tosa without pedigree — 1st category
approved_entry_points: No designated entry point for EU/EEA-origin movements — normal border crossings apply
rows.estimated_cost_range: EUR 12 I-CAD registration fee plus veterinary fees for the passport entry / rabies booster and the pre-travel clinical examination (typically EUR 50–150 per animal)
requirements: Dogs entering France from another EU Member State or from Norway/EEA under the intra-EU rules require: (1) ISO 11784/11785 microchip (or legible pre-3-July-2011 tattoo) implanted BEFORE vaccination; (2) valid rabies vaccination given at 12 weeks or older, valid from 21 days after the first injection, boosters up to date; (3) a valid EU pet passport issued by an authorised veterinarian, with section 10 clinical examination completed; (4) minimum age 15 weeks and at least one adult tooth; (5) registration with I-CAD within 7 days of arrival via a French veterinarian (EUR 12). No rabies titration test, no tapeworm treatment, no import permit, no quarantine. Maximum 5 animals per traveller for non-commercial movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events, after checking with the DDPP). 1st-category attack dogs are banned outright.
rows.notes: This is the rule set that applies to a Norway→France relocation: Norway is not treated as a third country for pet movements into the EU (EEA Joint Committee Decision No 66/2016; Regulation (EU) 2019/1293 recital 3), so the Norwegian EU-model pet passport is accepted and no titration test applies. The two steps movers most often miss are the mandatory I-CAD registration within 7 days of arrival and the fact that France's own minimum entry age is 15 weeks even though the vaccine may be given at 12 weeks. Tapeworm treatment is an outbound-to-Norway requirement, not an inbound-to-France one.

extras.clinical_exam_note: Section 10 (Examen clinique) of the passport must be completed. A clinical examination by a veterinarian authorised by the competent authority of the country of departure within 48 hours of travel is required for animals arriving from outside the EU; for intra-EU/EEA movements a good-health certificate shortly before arrival is the practice recommended by the French ministry.
extras.dangerous_dog_note: 1st-category 'chiens d'attaque' (the three types above, not entered in a recognised pedigree register) are totally prohibited from being brought into France — including mere transit through France. 2nd-category 'chiens de garde et de défense' may be brought in provided the French rules for that category are met (permis de détention from the mairie, muzzle and lead in public, third-party liability insurance — confirm the current requirements with the mairie of the commune of residence). A dog may only enter France if it has at least one adult tooth.
extras.icad_registration_note: NON-OBVIOUS STEP: a dog or cat brought into France must be registered in the national identification file I-CAD within 7 days of arrival. A veterinarian issues the 'certificat provisoire d'identification lors d'importation ou échange intracommunautaire' (valid one month) and can file it online with scanned supporting documents; the owner sends I-CAD a EUR 12 cheque. For an EU/Swiss-origin animal the supporting documents are photocopies of the passport sections for owner details, description, marking/identification, rabies vaccination, date of issue and section 10 (clinical examination). I-CAD: 29 rue du progrès, CS 50011, 93108 Montreuil Cedex, tel 09 77 40 30 77.

rows.rabies_vaccination_note: Valid only if the first injection was given at 12 weeks or older and after identification, and it takes effect 21 days later; boosters per the vaccine's periodicity.

rows.tapeworm_note: Never required for cats anywhere in the scheme, and not required for entry into France for any species.
rows.health_cert_type: Valid EU pet passport issued by an authorised veterinarian (Part 1 of Annex III to Regulation (EU) 577/2013), with section 10 clinical examination completed.
rows.quarantine_note: No quarantine for a compliant animal; official surveillance by prefectoral order is possible if the I-CAD registration reveals an anomaly.

No titration test, no tapeworm treatment, no permit, no quarantine, maximum 5 animals per traveller for non-commercial movement.

Crossbreeds morphologically assimilable to Mastiff / boerbull without pedigree — 1st category
Crossbreeds morphologically assimilable to Tosa without pedigree — 1st category

requirements: Dogs entering France from a non-EU country that is not exempted require: (1) minimum age 15 weeks; (2) ISO microchip or legible pre-2011 tattoo, implanted before vaccination; (3) valid rabies vaccination; (4) rabies antibody titration on a sample taken at least 30 days after vaccination and at least 3 months before arrival, at an EU-approved laboratory; (5) an animal health certificate from a veterinarian of the country of origin with the 48-hour clinical examination; (6) entry via a designated point of entry; (7) I-CAD registration within 7 days of arrival with the original health certificate. 1st-category attack dogs are banned.
rows.notes: This record is the fallback for origins outside the EU/EEA. It is NOT the Norway→France rule: Norway movements follow the intra-EU record above. The 3-month titration wait is the single biggest scheduling constraint on non-EU pet moves and must be started well before the move date.

rows.source_quote: Avoir fait l'objet d'une épreuve de titrage des anticorps antirabiques au moins 30 jours après la vaccination contre la rage et au moins 3 mois avant la date d'arrivée en France (examen sanguin effectué dans un laboratoire agréé par l'UE …). — Les animaux originaires de certains pays sont dispensés du titrage des anticorps antirabiques.
rows.review_reason: The list of countries exempted from the rabies titration test (Annex II to Regulation (EU) 577/2013, as amended) was not enumerated in this pass, and the designated travellers' points of entry were not enumerated per airport. Both should be confirmed against the current official lists before this record is shown to a customer.

extras.dangerous_dog_note: 1st-category attack dogs are prohibited from entering France, including in transit; 2nd-category dogs are admitted subject to the French detention rules.
extras.advance_notice_note: Third-country arrivals must enter through a designated travellers' point of entry and present the animal and its documents to the border control authorities — confirm the point of entry and any notification requirement with the airline and the DDPP before travel.
extras.icad_registration_note: I-CAD registration within 7 days of arrival. For a non-EU origin the supporting document is the ORIGINAL health certificate from the country of origin showing identification, rabies vaccination and the titration result — not passport photocopies.

rows.microchip_standard: ISO 11784 / ISO 11785 Annex A transponder (or legible pre-3-July-2011 tattoo); identification before vaccination.
rows.rabies_vaccination_note: First injection at 12 weeks or older and after identification; valid 21 days later.
rows.titre_test_note: Sample at least 30 days after vaccination and at least 3 months before arrival, at an EU-approved laboratory; animals from certain listed countries are exempt.
rows.tapeworm_note: Not required for cats, and not required for entry into France.
rows.health_cert_type: Identification document / animal health certificate from a veterinarian of the country of origin, with the clinical examination within 48 hours before travel.
approved_entry_points: Designated travellers' point of entry — verify the current list for the arrival airport
rows.estimated_cost_range: EUR 150–350 per animal (health certificate, titration test, clinical examination) plus the EUR 12 I-CAD fee
requirements: Cats entering France from a non-exempted non-EU country require minimum age 15 weeks, ISO identification before vaccination, valid rabies vaccination, rabies titration (30 days after vaccination, 3 months before arrival, EU-approved laboratory), an origin-country health certificate with the 48-hour clinical examination, entry via a designated point of entry, and I-CAD registration within 7 days of arrival.
rows.notes: Fallback record for non-EU/EEA origins. Not applicable to Norway→France moves, which follow the intra-EU record.
